summary: The evaluation covers the paper's empirical proximal finite-sum comparison, importance-resampled ProxRR variant, and federated FedRR comparison on the official real datasets.

claims.statement: On elastic-net logistic regression, ProxRR reaches the same order of objective accuracy as proximal SGD and the per-iteration proximal RR heuristic while evaluating the proximal operator once per data epoch instead of once per sample.
claims.comparison_conditions: Minibatch size 1, identical seed 42, 100 complete data epochs, theoretical smoothness-based initial step and O(1/t) decay.
planned_evidence: Formal history and metrics for all three methods

claims.statement: The importance-resampled ProxRR construction using n_i = ceil(L_i / mean(L_i)) is executable on a real sparse logistic problem and preserves one proximal evaluation per epoch while producing a same-order objective gap.
claims.comparison_conditions: Same elastic-net objective, seed 42, 100 epochs, and decay coefficient; only the finite-sum sampling construction differs.

claims.statement: On homogeneous federated data, FedRR converges faster than Local SGD when measured by communication rounds and processed data passes, including both full-pass and five-times shorter local budgets.
claims.comparison_conditions: Eight deterministic contiguous client shards, 140 rounds, theoretical step sizes, and minibatch size 8 as used by the official federated notebook.
planned_evidence: Unit test for client aggregation and round accounting
